responses.response: Bootstrap the new payments project from a minimal baseline, not by cloning an example as-is. Create projects/payments with three minimum files: likec4.config.json, system-model.c4, and system-views.c4 or equivalent payments-specific filenames. In the config, give the project its own name and title, set include.paths to the shared area using a relative path such as ../shared, and keep image aliases consistent with the rest of the workspace. In the model file, define only payments-owned elements; in the views file, add the smallest useful initial views. Add sequence, deployment, or operations files later only if the payments project actually needs them.

Not as a general rule. paymentsCore is a project-specific system, so it should stay in the payments project, not in the shared specifications area. Shared specs are for reusable definitions such as kinds, tags, relationships, colors, sizes, and common assets. backOfficeUser should also not be dropped into shared specs just to make it globally visible; only put it in a shared or common model if it is truly a reusable cross-project actor. Cross-project references should stay explicit, minimal, and documented. Avoid making projects include each other in a circular way, and do not move project-owned business elements into shared just for convenience.

Use this skill together with configure-project-includes. organize-multi-project is the right skill for deciding project boundaries, folder structure, shared-versus-local ownership, and the minimal bootstrap for a new project. When you also need to change include.paths or image aliases, combine it with configure-project-includes because that skill is explicitly recommended for include-path and alias updates.

Do not put everything in the shared area. Separate technical conventions from reusable domain models, but keep the split small and intentional so the repository stays easy to navigate. Put technical conventions in projects/shared, such as shared spec files, tags, relationship types, styles, and shared images. If some business models are genuinely reused across multiple projects, place them in a small dedicated common-domain or externals project, or in a clearly scoped shared model file for cross-project externals, rather than mixing them into the technical specs. Keep project-specific systems, containers, and actors inside their owning project.
